label: conj:gram-determinant-plancherel-ratio
title: Gram-determinant ratio $\kappa$ as a Plancherel-weighted character product
html:
Working over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}], let \beta_s = T_{2,9}, \beta_w = T_{3,5}. Each admits a Wedderburn decomposition into central idempotents of the ambient Hecke algebra H_n(R, q):

  \beta_\bullet \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    c_\lambda^{(\bullet)}\; e_\lambda,
  \qquad
  c_\lambda^{(\bullet)} \;=\; \chi_\lambda(\beta_\bullet) \in R.

Then the Gram-determinant ratio \kappa = \det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} / \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} appearing in the Chern-Simons descent (CS coupling) is given by a Plancherel-weighted character product of the form

  \boxed{\;
  \kappa \;=\;
  \prod_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    \left[
      \frac{\dim V_\lambda}{\dim_q V_\lambda}
      \cdot
      \frac{[n]_q!}{n!}
    \right]^{c_\lambda^{(s)}\, c_\lambda^{(w)}}
  \,\in\, R.
  \;}

The displayed product is not yet a well-defined element of R, and making it one is part of the conjecture. Two points are open: T_{2,9} is the closure of a braid on 2 strands and T_{3,5} of a braid on 3, so the two character families live on different Hecke algebras and the product over \lambda \vdash n needs a common n; and the exponents c_\lambda^{(s)} c_\lambda^{(w)} lie in R, not in \mathbb{Z}, so the powers are not defined in R. Nothing downstream uses this formula: the value \kappa \approx 1.7216 used in the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} form is computed directly from the two Gram determinants.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
heading: Conjecture
